chapter: Paris, Lester Young, drugs, Mississippi and later sessions
title: Henderson's band in Mississippi: the Rosedale sandwich shop
summary: On the road in Mississippi, a white man in Rosedale told Collins to stand outside because the place was too small for white folks and 'niggers.'

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: What was it like working with Fletcher Henderson's band in Mississippi? You said you couldn't wait to get out of there and didn't want to go back.

Oh, boy, oh, boy. Well, I'll give you an idea. I was in a little town, Rosedale we stopped, and I went into a little place to get a sandwich, so there was an old white man in there, and there was just the two of us. Nobody -- as a matter of fact no one was in there but him, and I went in and I ordered a ham sandwich, and I think a pork sandwich, and he started cutting the meat, slowly, you know. He was very -- I could see him thinking, I could see the wheels turning. This was an old man. So he finally just stuck the knife in the counter, he said, you'll just have to stand outside because this place is too small for white folks and niggers. That gives you an idea of what it was like, you know.
